land.text: Upper Egypt, where the 31st page says he revolted against Persian rule
Upper Egypt, which "returned to Persian control in 335 BC" (31st page)

capitals.name: Thebes (Luxor)
capitals.note: The page names no seat; a contract of his first year was written at Thebes and a decree has him go as king to Buto. Thebes is the researcher's reading.

rulers.name: Khababash (Senen-setepu-ni-ptah)
rulers.note: 31st page table 338–335; the Khababash page says ca. 338 BC and a revolt of "two or three years".

correction.text: Upper Egypt, which the 31st page table gives to Khababash while Artaxerxes IV "Only reigned in Lower Egypt"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Khababash page argues from a contract at Thebes, a decree naming Buto in the Delta and an Apis sarcophagus at Saqqara that he "really did have control over all, or almost all, of Egypt"; the 31st page table gives Upper Egypt only. The narrower shape is drawn (confidence 2); the wider claim is a disagreement between pages, recorded in the notes. No area.

ledger.note: 338: Khababash revolts and declares himself pharaoh. The 31st page table: "Led a revolt against Persian rule in Upper Egypt, declared himself Pharaoh", 338–335; the Khababash page: he "led a revolt against the Persian rule for two or three years from ca. 338 BC".
335: Persia recovers Upper Egypt. The 31st page table: "Upper Egypt returned to Persian control in 335 BC"; the Khababash page does not describe the end of his rule.
335: Khababash's rebel kingdom ends with the Persian recovery of Upper Egypt.

wars.name: Revolt of Khababash
wars.outcome: The rebel pharaoh held Upper Egypt for two or three years; Persian control returned in 335.
wars.note: The Khababash page says he "may have been of Libyan or Nubian descent" and, in a paraphrase of a Berlin stela, that a ruler called Kambasuten who may have been Khabash invaded Kush in the 330s and was defeated by King Nastasen; no dates are given.

certainty.note: No frontier is given by either page.

sources.title: Thirty-first Dynasty of Egypt
sources.note: Khababash 338–335 and the return of Upper Egypt in 335 (rulers table).

sources.title: Khababash
sources.note: Dating "ca. 338", Thebes, Buto and Saqqara evidence, Nubian descent.

notes: Rebel state (rule 5), three years, land held. The two pages disagree on the extent: the 31st page's table gives Upper Egypt to Khababash and Lower Egypt to Artaxerxes IV; the Khababash page concludes from a demotic contract at Thebes, a decree that has him go as king to Buto, and an Apis sarcophagus of his second year in the Serapeum at Saqqara that he held all or almost all of Egypt. Upper Egypt is drawn (the table's year and land); a reviewer who prefers the Khababash page should widen the keyframe to the whole Nile Valley and change the matching events in thirty-first-dynasty-of-egypt. The Khababash page gives no end of his rule and does not name the king he rebelled against ("Persian rule", and the 'enemy Xerxes' of the Ptolemy decree).
